As per the prosecution case, the marriage of deceased Anjali was solemnized with accused Mukesh Thakur and that being husband (accused Mukesh Thakur) and brothers in law (Sanjeev Thakur and State vs Mukesh Thakur Etc on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28010270/
1 Manish Thakur) alongwith co-accused (Meera Devi, mother in law, who is P.O.)
in furtherance of their common intention subjected injury to cruelty by making illegal demands of dowry and harassed her.
The accused persons have further criminally conspired to kill Anjali and in furtherance of their criminal conspiracy committed mother of Anjali.

As per case of prosecution, all the accused persons with co-accused Meera Devi and Mangal Kant (since P.O.) in furtherance of their common intention caused the evidence to disappear by cremating the body of deceased with intent to screen themselves from legal punishment.
2. This is pertinent to mention here that the accused Meera Devi and Mangal Kant were declared P.O. before the filing of the charge- sheet in this case.
3. The accused namely Mukesh Thakur was arrested on 28.11.2016 and accused Manish Thakur and Sanjeev Thakur both were arrested on 03.02.2017 during investigation.
The postmortem was conducted and no poison etc. was detected in the viscera of Anjali.
CHARGE 4.
Vide order dt. 23.08.2017, charges u/s.498A/34/120B/302/201 IPC & alternatively 304-B/34 IPC were framed against the accused persons.
The accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

iv) Sh. Manjul Gupta (PW-4) is the neighbor, who deposed that it was afternoon time around 02.00 P.M., when he was coming out, he observed that 3 persons were descending from the stairs from the second floor with something wrapped in the bed sheet.
That thereafter, he paused and again saw from the balcony that they had already put the wrapped material in Honda Amaze car, which was standing down.

it was deposed by him that on the fateful day, a Honda City Amaze of Delhi number (7827) was parked in the parking against a slip (Ex.PW5/A).
That after about 1-2 days, police came and seized the said car from the parking (vide seizure memo dt. 29.11.2016) and obtained the signature on some papers.

sentences.text: Ms. Anita Devi (PW-6) is the mother of the deceased, who has deposed that Anjali was her eldest daughter, who was married to accused Mukesh Thakur in May, 2015.

That only Mukesh and Anjali were residing in the house at Sec.22, Rohini.
That her daughter did not complaint to her at any point of time against her husband or any other person.
vii) Sh. Hirakant Jha (PW-7) is the maternal uncle (mama) of deceased Anjali.

It was deposed by him that he received phone call on 26.08.2016 or 27.08.2016 at 02.00 P.M. and pursuant to the said call, he left his work place with one of his colleague; that he made enquiry from the resident of top floor; that he also met with one lady under the said house, she told him that a lady was being taken wrapped in the cloth by 2-3 persons; that on being suspicion, he made a call at 100 number, P.C.R came and that he was instructed to PS Begum Pur and lodge the complaint; that at around 07.30-07.45 PM, he visited PS Begum Pur and lodged the missing report (Ex.PW1/A).

Out of 34 witnesses examined by the prosecution in this case, 6 are the material witnesses, who are the close relatives of the deceased which are as under:-

STATEMENT OF ACCUSED AND DEFENCE 8. Statement of accused persons were recorded on 15.03.2024 u/s 313 Cr.PC after putting all the incriminating evidence available on record.
The accused persons claimed innocence and denied the evidence.
The accused persons opted not to lead any defence evidence.
ARGUMENTS AND FINDINGS 9.
It is argued by Ld.
Defence counsel
that admittedly, the marriage of the deceased was solemnized in a mass marriage function.
That, there was no dowry demanded/exchanged either at the time of marriage or afterwards.
It is argued that nothing has been alleged by the accused persons constituting an offence u/s 498A, 304B or 302/201 IPC.
It is argued that the necessary ingredients of the charges have not been proved on record and the accused persons are entitled to be acquitted.

10. Section 498A IPC provides as under :-
Section 498A IPC. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.--Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation.--For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.]

11. The evidence of Smt. Anita Devi (PW-6), Sh. Hirakant Jha (PW- 7), Sh. Durga Nand Mishra (PW-20), Sh. Dharmender Mishra (PW-21), Sh. Dilip Kumar Mishra (PW-26) and Smt. Sunita (PW- 34) is the relevant and material to the case of the prosecution.
None of them has deposed anything incriminating against any of the accused.

sentences.text: After taking into account the nature of the comments/taunting, I am of the view that the same are manifestly falling short of cruelty within the meaning of explanation (a) of the Section 498A IPC.
13. Besides the above instances of general taunting, there is no further material on record to prove the charge u/s 498A IPC.

The evidence available on record is highly insufficient to bring home guilt u/s 498A IPC.
14.
I will now examine the charge u/s 304B IPC.

Section 304B provides as under:-
Section 304B. Dowry death.

-- (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for,
or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death", and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.

Explanation - For the purposes of this sub-section, "dowry" shall have the same meaning as in section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961).
(2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.]
15.

U/S 113 B of the Indian Evidence Act, a presumption of having caused the dowry death can be raised only if it is shown that soon before her death, such woman has been subjected by the accused to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with any demand for dowry.
16. As already discussed, the prosecution case has never been that there was any demand for dowry.
The marriage of Anjali was solemnized in a mass marriage function.
17. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel argued that the said annoyance, even if presumed to be true, cannot be treated as a dowry demand.

So far as charges u/s 302/201/34 IPC are concerned, nothing material has came on record against any of the accused in this case.
18.
I have considered the submissions and I have carefully gone through the evidence.
The marriage of Anjali was solemnized in May, 2015.
In absence of any proof of subjecting Anjali to cruelty or harassment for or in connection with any demand for dowry, soon before her death, the charge u/s 304B IPC has to fail.
19. For want of sufficient evidence, the charges could not be proved against any of the accused.

CONCLUSION State vs Mukesh Thakur Etc on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28010270/
7 20.

In view of the foregoing discussion, the accused Mukesh Thakur, Sanjeev Thakur and Manish Thakur are found not guilty and are accordingly, acquitted of the charges u/s.
498A/304B/302/201/34 IPC framed against them.
